", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u009-r0020", "tag": "p", "text": "“Well, let us start, and for how much?” the Jefe conceded wearily.", "sha256": "4effc9485f162b0adcab355450f96539b9a144b3c3def6a4dbdf70bbc5052408", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[656]", "source_html": "

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u009-r0021", "tag": "p", "text": "“Fifty dollars gold,” was the prompt answer.", "sha256": "8b94144c62476e6034b834240c0ae6fa125592f109fa52f485895999988d010a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[657]", "source_html": "

“Fifty dollars gold,” was the prompt answer.

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u009-r0022", "tag": "p", "text": "“You are starting anyway, are you not, Capitan?” Torres queried softly.", "sha256": "56f6433f11933197627f5f005952611ea6eb1c9e1140aa5b7cc3c45a0dbc0759", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[658]", "source_html": "

“Fifty——gold, as I have said.”

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u009-r0024", "tag": "p", "text": "The Jefe Politico threw up his hands with a hopeless gesture and turned on his heel to depart.", "sha256": "fbc3f28e32df397717c7c8e66e6f61fc01fdc407a08c0762b59947cb58b69112", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[660]", "source_html": "

The Jefe Politico threw up his hands with a hopeless gesture and turned on his heel to depart.

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u009-r0025", "tag": "p", "text": "“Yet you swore eternal vengeance for the crime committed on your jail,” Torres reminded him.", "sha256": "21d169762f9c23423e186d66dc06e31ff002ac0ca75f9351afb0e3b80ce5f7f6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[661]", "source_html": "

“Yet you swore eternal vengeance for the crime committed on your jail,” Torres reminded him.

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u009-r0026", "tag": "p", "text": "“But not if it costs fifty dollars,” the Jefe snapped back, out of the corner of his eye watching the shivering captain for some sign of relenting.", "sha256": "6b67999bc6ae42576cba3e1f43ab71bdfb0fa24074ace2bc26ee5ff7aa38aaaf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[662]", "source_html": "

It is our custom.”", "sha256": "782618c7638b84e90e40ad43cb4a2623c79821bd1163141ef015fc52d0562a06", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[663]", "source_html": "

Torres stepped closer to the Jefe and whispered:

As the sun slipped brazenly above the eastern horizon, one gendarme went back into Las Palmas with the jaded horses, the rest of the party descended to the deck of the tug, the Swede dived down into the engine-room, and Captain Rosaro, shaking off his chill in the sun’s beneficent rays, 71ordered the deck-hands to cast off the lines, and put one of them at the wheel in the pilot-house.

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u009-r0031", "tag": "p", "text": "And the same day-dawn found the [[I]]Angelique[[/I]], after a night of almost perfect calm, off the mainland from which she had failed to get away, although she had made sufficient northing to be midway between San Antonio and the passages of Bocas del Toro and Cartago. These two passages to the open sea still lay twenty-five miles away, and the schooner truly slept on the mirror surface of the placid lagoon. Too stuffy below for sleep in the steaming tropics, the deck was littered with the sleepers. On top the small house of the cabin, in solitary state, lay Leoncia. On the narrow runways of deck on either side lay her brothers and her father. Aft, between the cabin companionway and the wheel, side by side, Francis’ arm across Henry’s shoulder, as if still protecting him, were the two Morgans. On one side of the wheel, sitting, with arms on knees and head on arms, the negro-Indian skipper slept, and just as precisely postured, on the other side of the wheel, slept the helmsman, who was none other than Percival, the black Kingston negro. The waist of the schooner was strewn with the bodies of the mixed-breed seamen, while for’ard, on the tiny forecastlehead, prone, his face buried upon his folded arms, slept the lookout.", "sha256": "a2df45d677318317c3f0affe37be46bffcb27ec3792ffeb261058fc8fe06f53d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[667]", "source_html": "

And the same day-dawn found the Angelique, after a night of almost perfect calm, off the mainland from which she had failed to get away, although she had made sufficient northing to be midway between San Antonio and the passages of Bocas del Toro and Cartago. These two passages to the open sea still lay twenty-five miles away, and the schooner truly slept on the mirror surface of the placid lagoon. Too stuffy below for sleep in the steaming tropics, the deck was littered with the sleepers. On top the small house of the cabin, in solitary state, lay Leoncia. On the narrow runways of deck on either side lay her brothers and her father. Aft, between the cabin companionway and the wheel, side by side, Francis’ arm across Henry’s shoulder, as if still protecting him, were the two Morgans. On one side of the wheel, sitting, with arms on knees and head on arms, the negro-Indian skipper slept, and just as precisely postured, on the other side of the wheel, slept the helmsman, who was none other than Percival, the black Kingston negro. The waist of the schooner was strewn with the bodies of the mixed-breed seamen, while for’ard, on the tiny forecastlehead, prone, his face buried upon his folded arms, slept the lookout.
